records.habit: Soft-wooded, stellate-pubescent shrub 0.7–3 m with widely spreading branches
records.leaves: Petioles to 38 mm; aromatic elliptic–ovate blades 8–23 cm long, sharply toothed
records.flowers: Axillary cymes; small funnel-shaped 4-lobed corollas lavender-pink to bluish, reddish or white; corolla tube 2.6–2.9 mm
records.fruits: Drupaceous, strongly clustered, rose-pink through violet/red-purple, globose 3–6 mm diameter, spicy odor
records.note: Modern repository assigns Lamiaceae; historical source places this genus in Verbenaceae.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Aromatic shrub or small tree to 5 m
records.leaves: Opposite palmately compound leaves with (3–)5–9 leaflets, to ca. 12 cm long, dark above and white-puberulent beneath; petioles to 75 mm
records.flowers: Dense inflorescences to 31 cm; calyx 2–2.5 mm, corolla tube 6–7 mm, limb to 13 mm wide; Vitex generic treatment has 4 stamens, bilabiate flowers
records.fruits: Drupaceous and somewhat fleshy per genus treatment
records.habitat: Introduced ornamental, escaping/naturalizing in moist habitats and waste places
records.note: Flora distinguishes varieties agnus-castus and caerulea mainly by flower color; source places genus in Verbenaceae; current family Lamiaceae.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Erect annual 7–45(–75) cm, simple or widely branched
records.leaves: Mostly sessile, slightly clasping oblong–oblanceolate blades to 70 × 23 mm, toothed toward apex
records.flowers: Terminal spike-like racemes; bracts 3–6 mm, puberulent calyces 3–5 mm becoming to 7.9 mm and closed in fruit; pinkish to lavender corollas 8.5–12 mm with pale, purple-dotted throat; 4 stamens
records.fruits: Conspicuously 3-angled nutlets yellow maturing brown and gold
records.habitat: Gravelly or thin clay soils on limestone
records.note: 1999 authors acknowledge generic recognition versus possible placement within Brazoria.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Much-branched shrub to 3 m; young twigs minutely pubescent
records.leaves: Opposite green lanceolate/elliptic/narrow-oblong blades 3–27 × 2–8 mm, usually entire or 1–4 teeth each side; often smaller axillary leaf fascicles
records.flowers: Sweet vanilla-scented flowers in peduncled upright dense spike-like racemes 2–7 cm; white or violet-tinged corolla with green-yellow eye, tube ca. 3.5 mm, limb 3.5 mm across
records.note: Flora treats species broadly while describing morphological differences for varieties gratissima and schulziae.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.leaves: Opposite, variable and 1–2 pinnatifid per flora key
records.flowers: Bracts usually exceed calyces; calyx generally non-glandular pubescent or few glandular hairs; pink, lavender or purple salverform corolla; flora key tube usually 10–15 mm, limb 7–10(–15) mm; calyx 7–10 mm
records.habitat: Disturbed areas, mainly western two-thirds of Texas
records.flowering: Late Mar–Jun, less freely to Oct
records.note: Generic placement historically contrasted with Verbena using nutlets and chromosome numbers.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Low annual with decumbent/spreading to erect stems, hirsute and often finely glandular
records.flowers: Spikes sessile or short-peduncled; pink to lavender or pale blue corolla, rarely white; key: corolla tube 8–10 mm, limb 3–5 mm across; calyx ca. 6 mm
records.fruits: Genus 4 nutlets; key nutlet length 2–2.8 mm
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Unarmed or sparsely armed shrub to 2 m
records.leaves: Broad, cordate/triangular ovate, fine crenate teeth 0.5–1.5 mm; stem angles short recurved rather than long hispid hairs (key)
records.flowers: Dense axillary heads on long peduncles; narrow triangular-lanceolate bractlets usually shed before fruit; corolla tube ca. 10 mm; genus 4 stamens
records.habitat: Cultivated and escaped, particularly southern/central Texas; historically reported from Bell County
records.note: Flora uses broad L. camara; horticultural hybrid Lantana × strigocamara is separately inventoried and should not be automatically synonymized or conflated.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Armed or unarmed shrub to 2 m
records.leaves: Ovate to broadly ovate, upper surface strongly scabrous; coarse marginal teeth 2–5 mm (source key)
records.flowers: Bractlets 4–9 × 1–2 mm, persistent, oblanceolate/spatulate (key); flowers yellow or orange changing red; corolla tube 7–10 mm, limb 5–9 mm wide
records.habitat: Open areas, thickets, woods and roadsides; source says native central/southern Texas, but BONAP county proof pending
records.note: Flora warns potential hybridization with L. camara.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Creeping or trailing to ascending perennial, rooting at nodes per family key
records.leaves: Oblanceolate widest near apex, length 10–72 mm, mostly toothed only near apex; key width 4–25 mm
records.flowers: Flowers in short axillary heads on peduncles 1.5–4× adjacent leaf length; heads 6–10 mm thick elongating to 3 cm in fruit; corollas white to rose-purple often yellow-eyed; floral bracts small 2–3 mm
records.fruits: Genus treatment fruits split into two nutlets at maturity
records.note: 1999 flora explicitly chooses Lippia over segregate Phyla. Identification warning: Lippia/Phyla canescens should remain separate; bract and calyx hairs are diagnostic.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.flowers: Slender elongate spikes; calyx 2.5–3 mm; corolla blue to pink/lavender, tube approximately equals calyx, limb ca. 2 mm wide
records.habitat: Low ground; flora notes few TX specimens actually seen despite broad secondary reports
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

taxonomic_review.issue: Callicarpa and Vitex placed in Verbenaceae by 1999 flora but assigned to Lamiaceae by active repository
taxonomic_review.action: retain both family names, no route change
record flora name and current repository name separately
do not equate cultivar/hybrid material with source species treatment

bonap_county_verification: pending for all; no local native labels established from 1999 flora
